description: Machine-readable form of Table 8 (detailed experimental testbed configuration) and the evaluation design constants stated in Section 3 of the companion paper. JSON is used so that the framework needs no third-party packages.
source: EDR-EvadeBench companion paper, Table 8 and Section 3

payload_families.note: widely used commercial framework with extensive public signature coverage
modern open-source framework with an evolving detection landscape
lightweight, less prevalent framework; tests generalisation beyond well-known tools

hardware.host_cpu: 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700, base frequency 3.40 GHz, 16 cores / 24 threads
hardware.host_ram: 32.0 GB DDR5 4800 MT/s; two Windows virtual machines allocated 8 GB memory each
hardware.vm_storage: Each virtual machine equipped with an 80 GB NVMe virtual disk
hardware.hypervisor: VMware Workstation 17 Pro (Build 17.6.1-24319023, personal use license)

network.adapter: Intel(R) 82574L Gigabit Network Connection, DHCP enabled
network.c2: Ubuntu C2 server using an RFC 1918 private address within the isolated virtual network; no public-facing listener or domain name
network.automatic_sample_submission: Disabled for all evaluated products throughout the evaluation
network.address_policy: Machine roles only; original guest, gateway and DNS addresses are not publicly distributed.

levels.name: Pre-execution Prevention
levels.definition: The product blocks the sample before any process is created.

levels.name: Pre-C2 Prevention
levels.definition: The process runs, but the product terminates it before a C2 connection is established within the timeout period.

levels.name: Pre-command Prevention
levels.definition: The C2 connection is established, but the product terminates the session before any command is sent.

levels.name: Command-stage Prevention
levels.definition: Commands are sent, but they do not complete successfully, or the session is terminated within the timeout period.

levels.name: Operational Success
levels.definition: All commands execute successfully and the session remains alive throughout the timeout period.

evidence_sources: product alerts or local protection logs
outcome_model.note: Each level is mutually exclusive. Outcomes are determined by correlating the three evidence sources.

protocol.payload_protection: Same AES-based encryption and runtime decryption procedure for T0 and T1-T22.
protocol.repetition_rule: Each case is repeated until five consecutive executions yield the same outcome; that outcome is recorded as the final result.
protocol.snapshot_policy: Both the target VM and the Ubuntu C2 server are reverted to clean snapshots before every execution; both VMs are fully powered off after each test.
protocol.retained_logs: Original screenshots and full logs are retained internally because they contain sensitive environment information. The public results contain one final label per case and do not include complete historical per-execution traces.
protocol.source_payload_buffer_format: AES-based encryption with runtime decryption; payload buffer format is [16-byte IV] + AES-256-CBC ciphertext
protocol.product_configuration: Default product protection configurations; automatic sample submission disabled.
protocol.implementation_version: First adapted implementation version used throughout the reported evaluation; no code revisions during evaluation.

baseline.description: Payloads from Cobalt Strike, Havoc and AdaptixC2 with the same AES-based encryption and runtime decryption as T1-T22, but no additional evasion mechanism.
baseline.result: All 36 baseline outcomes (six products x three payload families x two environments) were classified as L1 (Pre-execution Prevention).
